title: Pampers Baby Dry Gr. 4 vs Jeden Tag Babywindeln Maxi Gr. 4

brand.product: Pampers Baby Dry Windeln Gr. 4, 9-14 kg, 34 nappies

alternative.product: Jeden Tag Babywindeln Maxi Gr. 4, 9-14 kg, 42 nappies

summary: Two size 4 nappies for the same 9-14 kg weight at one shop, with Jeden Tag about half the price per nappy.
evidence: mytime.de lists Pampers Baby Dry Gr. 4 (34) at €11.59 and Jeden Tag Maxi Gr. 4 (42) at €7.09, both with VAT and plus shipping, read in November 2026. Pampers' 78-pack is €25.45, about 33 cents a nappy, still dearer than Jeden Tag. Stiftung Warentest (08/2021) put Pampers Baby-Dry size 4 at 21 cents and store brands from dm, Edeka and Lidl at 12 to 13 cents. Those are older prices and Jeden Tag was not in that test.
differences: The Pampers page describes a wetness indicator, double leg cuffs and a back pocket against leaks, and an OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100 certificate. The Jeden Tag page mentions none of these. No test we could read covers Jeden Tag, and the grades in the Stiftung Warentest and Öko-Test nappy tests are behind a paywall, so we can't say how they compare on leaks or fit.
why: Same size and weight range at one shop, for about half the price per nappy. Buy one pack first, because leaks and fit are the part we have no test for.

title: Pampers Feuchte Tücher Sensitive vs Jeden Tag Baby Feuchttücher sensitiv

brand.product: Pampers Feuchte Tücher Sensitive, 3 x 80 wipes

alternative.product: Jeden Tag Baby Feuchttücher sensitiv, 2 x 80 wipes

summary: Two sensitive baby wipes without added perfume at one shop, with Jeden Tag well under half the price per wipe.
evidence: mytime.de lists Pampers Sensitive (3 x 80) at €7.29 and Jeden Tag sensitiv (2 x 80) at €2.06, both with VAT and plus shipping, read in November 2026. Öko-Test's fragrance-free wipes test (published 2025, bought June and July 2024) priced Pampers Sensitive at €1.71 for 80 wipes, and most store-brand sensitive wipes between €0.86 and €1.30.
differences: The ingredient lists differ, and Jeden Tag adds aloe, chamomile, panthenol and glycerin. Pampers says on its page that dermatologists of the Skin Health Alliance confirmed it and that it suits newborns' skin. Jeden Tag says dermatologically confirmed, pH-neutral and perfume-free. Jeden Tag was not in the Öko-Test list, and its grades are behind a paywall. We did not compare wipe size or thickness.
why: Both are sold as sensitive and perfume-free at the same shop, and Pampers costs more than twice as much per wipe. Öko-Test's price list shows a similar gap against other store brands.

title: Bübchen Baby Shampoo sensitiv vs Penaten Baby Shampoo
summary: Two baby shampoos at one shop, with Penaten's bigger bottle about a quarter cheaper per ml.
evidence: mytime.de lists Bübchen sensitiv (200 ml) at €2.25 and Penaten (400 ml) at €3.45, both with VAT and plus shipping, read in November 2026. Both labels say dermatologically tested and both contain perfume.
differences: The cleansing ingredients differ. Bübchen's page says its mildness to eyes is confirmed by eye doctors, and it adds panthenol, aloe and chamomile. Penaten's page says it is as mild to the eyes as pure water. Penaten is a big name too, so this is a cheaper brand rather than a budget product, and you have to buy twice as much. No test we could read covers this pair.
why: Both are baby shampoos with dermatological claims and perfume on the label, and buying the bigger Penaten bottle costs less per ml.

title: Hakle Feucht Ultra med vs Jeden Tag Feuchtes Toilettenpapier sensitiv

brand.product: Hakle Feucht Toilettenpapier Ultra med, 42 sheets

alternative.product: Jeden Tag Feuchtes Toilettenpapier sensitiv, 70 sheets

summary: Two moist toilet tissues at one shop, with Jeden Tag less than a third of the price per sheet.
evidence: mytime.de lists Hakle Feucht Ultra med (42) at €1.95 and Jeden Tag sensitiv (70) at €0.99, both with VAT and plus shipping, read in November 2026. Ingredients are from both product pages.
differences: Hakle's page cites a slosh-box test for dissolving in water, and says it is biodegradable and free of microplastic. Jeden Tag's page says it can go down the toilet, no more than two sheets at a time, but cites no test. Hakle has witch hazel. Jeden Tag has aloe and chamomile and says it is perfume-free. why: Same job, both with panthenol and both flushable by their own labels. If flushing matters to your pipes, Hakle is the one that cites a test.

title: Lenor Weichspüler Aprilfrisch vs Jeden Tag Weichspüler Meeresfrische

alternative.product: Jeden Tag Weichspüler Meeresfrische, 1.5 l, 75 washes

summary: Two liquid fabric softeners at one shop with about the same dose, with Jeden Tag well under half the price per wash.
evidence: mytime.de lists Lenor Aprilfrisch (71 washes) at €5.79 and Jeden Tag Meeresfrische (75 washes, 1.5 l) at €2.29, both with VAT and plus shipping, read in November 2026. Stiftung Warentest's softener test (10/2019) found only 6 of 21 good, costs of 2 to 15 cents a wash, and the most expensive product failing to soften at all.
differences: The scents differ. Neither of these two was shown in the part of the 2019 test we read, and that test is old. Lenor's page warns against use on children's nightwear and flame-retardant clothing, because liquid softeners can raise flammability. We did not see that warning on the Jeden Tag page, but read the label for either.
why: The dose is nearly the same and the label bands show softening agents in both. Stiftung Warentest's 2019 test found that the highest price did not buy softness.

title: Demak'Up Expert Wattepads vs La Ligne Duo Wattepads

title: Persil Universal Kraft-Gel vs Jeden Tag Vollwaschmittel flüssig
summary: Two liquid full-wash detergents with the same label bands at one shop, with Jeden Tag about half the price per wash.
evidence: mytime.de lists Persil Universal Kraft-Gel (20 washes) at €7.89 and Jeden Tag Vollwaschmittel flüssig (27 washes) at €5.05, both with VAT and plus shipping, read in November 2026. Both pages state 5-15% anionic and nonionic surfactants, enzymes and optical brighteners.
differences: Label bands are ranges, so the same band does not mean the same amount. Persil's page gives a dose of 45 ml for 4-5 kg. We found no dose for Jeden Tag, so its wash count is the maker's own figure. No test we could read covers these two liquids.
why: The label shows the same ingredient bands and the same types of ingredient, at about half the price per wash at one shop. No wash test covers them, so we can't say the results match.

title: Pampers Harmonie Aqua vs Tesco Fred & Flo Biodegradable Wipes

brand.product: Pampers Harmonie Aqua baby wipes, 48 wipes

alternative.product: Tesco Fred & Flo Biodegradable Fragrance Free wipes, 60 wipes

summary: Two fragrance-free baby wipes in Which?'s price table, with Fred & Flo about 1p a wipe against about 5p for Pampers.
evidence: Which? listed Pampers Harmonie Aqua (48) at £2.55 with a link to Boots and Tesco Fred & Flo (60) at 59p with a link to Tesco, prices correct on 5 March 2026. Which? does not say which shop each price is from, so the shops are from its links. No ingredient list in its table includes a fragrance.
differences: This is more than an 80% saving, and we checked the packs: 48 and 60 wipes. The formulas are not the same. Fred & Flo has the longest list in the table, at 17 ingredients, and contains phenoxyethanol. Pampers has seven. Which? shows Fred & Flo as biodegradable and Not stated for Pampers. Which? compared prices and ingredients only and did not test how well they clean.
why: Both clean a baby without added fragrance, for very different money. If you want a shorter ingredient list, Pampers has one.

why: If a short list is why you buy WaterWipes, Superdrug's list is one of the shorter ones in the table and is biodegradable too, for a third less. WaterWipes' list is still the shorter of the two.

title: Pampers Baby-Dry Size 4 vs Tesco Fred & Flo Ultra Dry Size 4

alternative.product: Tesco Fred & Flo Ultra Dry Size 4, 48 nappies

summary: Which?'s price tracking puts Pampers Baby-Dry size 4 at 25p a nappy at Tesco and Tesco's own at about 6p.
evidence: Which? tracked prices from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. At Tesco, Pampers Baby-Dry size 4 (44) averaged £11 with a low of £11, 25p a nappy. Tesco Fred & Flo Ultra Dry size 4 (48) averaged £2.89, 6.02p a nappy. Prices include regular discounts but not multibuys or loyalty prices. Pampers averaged 17p a nappy at Asda, one of its cheapest shops over that year, so the gap can be smaller.
differences: Which? tests nappies in its lab, but the scores for these two are for members only and we have not seen them. Which? says budget supermarket nappies range from 88% to 67% in its tests and one of Aldi and Lidl does much better than the other, so own-label quality varies. We did not read the Fred & Flo weight range, and the Open Products Facts record we cite for the range shows a different size.
why: Pampers costs about four times as much per nappy at the same shop. Which?'s scores show budget nappies vary, so try one pack before stocking up.
